listings.title: Aarohi Batik Silk Saree
listings.description: Batik is a wax-resist technique: wax is drawn or stamped onto the fabric, the fabric is dyed, and then the wax is removed. Repeating this builds up layered patterns. In India, Shantiniketan batik from West Bengal has GI recognition.

listings.title: Dhara Khadi Saree
listings.description: Khadi is natural-fibre cloth that's spun and woven by hand. It's usually cotton, sometimes silk or wool. Gandhi promoted it during the Swadeshi movement, and it's a symbol of self-reliance and support for artisans. The texture is slightly coarse and uneven because it's handmade. It stays cool in summer and warm in winter.

listings.title: Gajraj Madras Checks Saree
listings.description: A light cotton with plaid-style checks, and authentic madras shows the same pattern on both sides. Short-staple cotton gives it small, uneven bumps called slubs. Colours can "bleed," which is a well-known feature of the fabric. I couldn't find out what "Gajraj" means here. It's probably a design or colour name used by Pehchaan.'

listings.title: Katha Mul Cotton Kalamkari Saree
listings.description: The name means "pen-craft." It comes from Andhra Pradesh and has two protected regional (GI) styles. Srikalahasti: painted freehand with a pen, showing scenes from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and Hindu gods. Machilipatnam: block-printed with vegetable dyes, with Persian-influenced motifs like vines, peacocks and the tree of life. The process can take up to 23 steps and uses natural dyes, with myrobalan and alum to set the colours. In the "Border Pallu" version, the Kalamkari work is probably only on the border and pallu, with a plainer body.

listings.title: Madhav Madras Checks Saree
listings.description: Madras cloth is named after Chennai. It's a light cotton with plaid-style checks, and authentic madras shows the same pattern on both sides. Short-staple cotton gives it small, uneven bumps called slubs. Colours can "bleed," which is a well-known feature of the fabric. I couldn't find out what "Gajraj" means here. It's probably a design or colour name used by Pehchaan.

listings.title: Madhavi Mul Cotton Saree
listings.description: Mulmul is a fine, plain-weave cotton muslin with Bengal roots, especially around Dhaka. It's soft, thin, slightly see-through, very light and breathable, which makes it a good everyday summer saree.

listings.title: Mogra Printed Mul Cotton Saree

listings.title: Nazaakat Raw Silk Saree
listings.description: In Indian saree shopping, "raw silk" usually means silk that has a slightly rough, slubby texture, a crisp drape and a softer, less glossy sheen than finished silk. Wikipedia's closest page, on "silk noil," describes a similar low-sheen, slightly rough silk that's gaining popularity for sarees in India. That page isn't exactly about raw silk, though.

listings.description: Feather Silk, An ivory silk edged in a bold pink flame border, the pallu opening into a Kalamkari-style scene of peacocks, temple houses and vines in teal, pink and gold. Feather silk keeps the whole piece light enough for a full evening's wear.

listings.title: The Pari
listings.description: Semi Satin, Steel-blue and mauve run in bold diagonal stripes across this silk, bordered in gold-flecked brocade. Semi satin gives the sharp geometry a gentle, wearable sheen.

listings.title: The Pihu
listings.description: Feather Silk, Rose pink meets emerald green in a Paithani-inspired weave, its pallu given over entirely to a procession of woven peacocks. Feather silk lets the colour-blocking read crisp and architectural rather than heavy.

listings.title: The Radhika
listings.description: Linen Silk, A soft blush pink Banarasi, paisleys and floral medallions woven in muted rose and sage across the body and border. Linen silk gives it a matte, understated finish, quiet luxury rather than shine.

listings.title: The Riya
listings.description: Semi Satin, The same diagonal chevron weave in a softer rose pink, the gold border catching the light at every turn. Semi satin keeps it light and easy to wear well past the occasion that called for it.

listings.title: The Sanaya
listings.description: Linen Silk, The same paisley Banarasi reworked in a fresh mint green, the florals picked out in coral and gold for warmth. Linen silk keeps the drape light and matte, easy to wear from morning through evening.

listings.title: The Trisha
listings.description: Linen Silk, A cool silver-grey Banarasi with the identical paisley brocade, its rose-and-teal florals reading almost jewel-like against the pale base. Linen silk's soft hand keeps the overall look restrained and elegant.

listings.title: The Urvi
listings.description: Feather Silk, A gold silk striped through with bold lavender-and-olive chevrons, woven in an ikat technique that blurs each edge softly. Feather silk keeps the geometry light rather than stiff, so the saree moves rather than stands still.

listings.title: The Vidhi
listings.description: Feather Silk, The same chevron ikat in a cooler palette, dusty blue and mauve zigzagging across warm gold. Feather silk's lightness lets the pattern ripple naturally with every step.

listings.title: The Yamini
listings.description: Semi Satin, A warm rust-orange silk scattered with small gold motifs, finished in a deep border of woven peacocks, florals and vines. Semi satin gives it a gentle, low-key sheen, festive without being loud.

listings.title: The Zoya
listings.description: Semi Satin, The same peacock-bordered design in a rich sea green, gold accents picked out across the body like scattered light. Semi satin lends it a soft glow that reads well both indoors and out.
